findings.body: On Windows, a failed Get-CimInstance query can leave $p empty and continue to `exit 3`; `gone` then treats the owner as absent even when stderr reports a lookup failure. PowerShell's default error behavior permits this continuation ([documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_commonparameters#erroraction)). If this occurs while checking an existing owner, `_take` deletes its live lock. A second work can enter, or doctor can stop the active worker's Codex processes. Distinguish query failures from successful queries returning no process, and return an unknown identity on failure.
findings.title: Not done: 5. Unidentifiable owners count as running

findings.body: `emit(pid=...)` only writes to a pipe; the driver immediately continues toward `thread_start` without waiting for Forge to save the identity. Meanwhile, codex.py:175–176 still needs to receive the message, run ps/PowerShell, and atomically write the record. A delayed identity lookup therefore allows a conversation and turn to start while the record still has `app_server: null`. Emitting the thread ID has the same unsynchronized persistence gap. Require acknowledgement of successful recording before advancing, and test with the recorder delayed rather than initialization stalled.
findings.title: Not done: 5. Record the process before starting any conversation

findings.body: Installing/checking the SDK under a Claude coordinator is separate cold-reader setup work; process recovery through `codex.tidy` does not require it. This extension adds unnecessary changes to the out-of-scope tests/test_codex_setup.py and tests/conftest.py. The tests/test_setup.py changes likewise support unrelated doctor wording changes. Remove those setup and wording changes from this part while retaining the lifecycle integration and its tests.
findings.title: Simpler: unrelated doctor setup changes → existing setup behavior
